display_name: Isle of Skye 21 Year Old (Blended Scotch, Ian Macleod)
cask: Blend of peated island malts matched with Speyside and Highland malts plus grain whiskies. Specific cask regime N/A — not found (TWW notes 'Chestnut/Oloroso sherry' colour only).
outturn_or_availability: Ongoing core-range expression; not limited. 70cl. SRP US$114.99.

tasting.nose: Warm baking spices, red apples, buttery toffee, citrus and chocolate malted balls; a beautiful dry nuttiness with brown sugar, vanilla, cedar chest, nutmeg, cinnamon, dried citrus, coffee and walnut cake.
tasting.palate: Subtle stone-fruit sweetness — spicy caramel, blackcurrant, chocolate, lemon zest, a hint of cedar wood and green peppercorn; sweet and honeyed with hot oatmeal, chocolate sauce, strawberries, orange and a whirl of ground pepper and oak spice.
tasting.finish: Medium to long, deliciously rich and oaky, with a glimpse of peppermint.
tasting.narrative: The entry point to Isle of Skye's older blends: a smooth, medium-bodied, easy-sipping island blend that trades sweet orchard and confectionery notes against savoury nuttiness and gentle oak rather than chasing complexity. The Whiskey Wash calls it 'a subtly decadent treat'; Whisky Advocate's Jonny McCormick praised its dry nuttiness. Curator verdict: a well-made, approachable aged blend at a fair price — pleasant rather than profound.
